clue.text: 17 over 25 20 somehow compromise eg full noses

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of the following words are put together in some new way

explanation.surface: A cryptic instruction to rework a compromise involving full noses, framed around other entries in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges COMPROMISE EG FULL NOSES (21 letters). The definition uses the grid: PREVAILING (17) over A STAIN ON ONE'S CHARACTER (25, 20), i.e. emerging from a scandal with reputation intact.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes escaping a potentially damaging episode with one's reputation unharmed, triumphing over any slur.

clue.text: Over time, state intrudes typically!

indicators.note: intrudes means the word for state pushes its way into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: on can mean over, as in resting on top of
an age is a period of time
to aver is to state or declare

explanation.surface: A remark that the state usually encroaches over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done typically is done as a rule, in the usual or mean way, as an average case.

clue.text: The see's without an archdeacon; that's on the level!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the see's name goes round the archdeacon

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and diocese, a bishop's see
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A diocese lacking an archdeacon, which is pronounced to be fair and square.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'without' as lacking, but in its old sense it means outside, so the see's name is split around the archdeacon's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lying evenly is flat and level, as a surface is when it is on the level.

clue.text: Pain alert issued around the delivery time

indicators.note: issued suggests the letters are sent out and come out in a different form

explanation.surface: A warning of labour pains given as a birth approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issued' rearranges PAIN ALERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Perinatal is the medical term for the period immediately before and after childbirth.

clue.text: Deserted the Queen Mother? Not her, him!

parts.note: D is a record-keeping abbreviation for deserted
ER, for Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

indicators.note: not her tells us the letters of the word her are removed from the word before

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether someone abandoned the Queen Mother, answered by saying it was a man rather than a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: MOTHER without HER leaves MOT. The definition 'him' is just a man's name, cheekily contrasted with 'her'.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a male Irish first name, so it can stand for a man, a him.

clue.text: Still follow the game in Japan?

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
go is a board game of Japanese origin

explanation.surface: A question whether someone continues to keep up with a sport played in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like 'even now', but it means motionless, as in 'lying doggo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying doggo is British slang for keeping quiet and motionless to avoid notice, staying still.

clue.text: Tired and emotional to get into this state?

definitions.text: Tired and emotional to get into this state?

parts.words: Tired and emotional to get into this state
parts.note: tired is read as fitted with tyres, so a driver on wheels getting emotional gets into a furious state on the highway

explanation.surface: A question about whether fatigue and drink lead to an outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tired and emotional' is a British euphemism for drunk, but here 'tired' means on tyres, i.e. in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Road rage is violent anger shown by a driver towards other road users, an emotional state on wheels.

clue.text: Make sighs, say, to do as the wolf does!

definitions.meaning: makes eyes, run together and spoken, sounds like make sighs; making eyes at someone is staring amorously

definitions.text: to do as the wolf does
definitions.meaning: a wolf in slang is a womaniser who stares lustfully at women

explanation.surface: Advice to sigh dramatically, in the manner of a wolf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that 'make sighs' is heard as 'makes eyes'.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer at someone with amorous interest is to make eyes at them, as a predatory womaniser would.

clue.text: Couple in a primal embrace, one doing it for love

indicators.note: embrace means the outer pieces wrap their arms round the word for couple

parts.note: ur- is a prefix meaning primitive or original, so primal
to mate is to couple or pair

explanation.surface: Two people locked in a primitive hug, one of them motivated by love.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the Latin root amator, lover; 'in' is a link word here, while 'embrace' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur, from Latin amator, a lover, pursues an activity for enjoyment rather than for payment.

clue.text: First responder when a person is otherwise engaged

definitions.text: First responder when a person is otherwise engaged

parts.words: First responder when a person is otherwise engaged
parts.note: first responder sounds like an emergency worker, but means the device that picks up the call first when the person phoned is busy

explanation.surface: An emergency worker attending while someone is occupied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First responder' wants to be paramedics and fire crews; the clue is about a telephone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that records messages takes calls when the owner is unavailable, responding before the person does.

clue.text: The Trotter boy called back, "Get knotted!"

indicators.note: back says the combined pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: Del Boy Trotter is the wheeler-dealer in the British TV sitcom Only Fools and Horses
rang means called on the telephone

explanation.surface: The sitcom character phoned back and told someone to get lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DELRANG into GNARLED. 'Get knotted' is British slang for 'go away', but here 'knotted' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnarled wood or hands are twisted and knobbly, covered in knots.

clue.text: Wouldn't cash the cheque, bringing ruin on the Guardian's boss

parts.note: to dishonour can mean to ruin someone's reputation or a woman's virtue
ED, the editor, is the boss of a newspaper such as the Guardian

explanation.surface: A bank refused a cheque, ruining the newspaper's editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing ... on' is the linking frame; the cheque sense and the ruin sense of the same verb meet in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank that dishonours a cheque refuses to pay out on it, typically for lack of funds.

clue.text: See 1
The old get around like a young hawk

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the old word for the round the other way

parts.note: ye is an old form of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe
as means like

explanation.surface: Elderly people move about like a young bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyas is a young hawk taken from the nest for training in falconry.

clue.text: One's racehorses finish with nothing; need order to go faster!

parts.note: a string is the set of racehorses owned or trained by one person
end means finish
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A trainer's horses come in last; they need ordering to speed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces and 'need' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringendo is a musical direction telling performers to quicken the tempo, an instruction to accelerate.

clue.text: Odysseus's ambit? That is a case for over one solution

indicators.note: case for means the first pieces form a casing round the following ones

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
on can mean over, as in placed on top
I is the Roman numeral one
ANS is the abbreviation of answer, a solution

explanation.surface: A question about the range of the Greek hero, which supposedly encloses one answer.
explanation.walkthrough: IE+A splits after its I to wrap ONIANS. The ? marks a definition by example: Odysseus sailed home to Ithaca, an island in this sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus's home island of Ithaca lies in this stretch of the Mediterranean west of Greece, so it was his territory.

clue.text: Close call? Close it!

parts.note: near means close
it can mean a thing, as in 'what is it?'

explanation.surface: A question about a narrow escape, answered with an order to shut something.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'Close' looks like a verb meaning shut, but it is the adjective near.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape, where disaster was only just avoided, is a close-run situation.

clue.text: Spanish port — Cava mixed with Nile output

indicators.note: mixed says the letters of the two words are blended together

explanation.surface: A Spanish harbour city producing sparkling wine blended with Egyptian river water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges CAVA and NILE; 'with' and 'output' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a major Mediterranean port city on Spain's east coast.

clue.text: Two priests sick, but gaining strength

parts.note: P is an abbreviation for priest
Rev, short for Reverend, is a priest's title
ailing means sick

explanation.surface: A pair of clergymen are ill, yet getting stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: The two priests are two different abbreviations: P and REV.
explanation.definitionFit: Prevailing forces are winning out, gaining the upper hand and growing dominant.

clue.text: One by one by Shakespeare

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
by can mean past, as in days gone by, which is ago

explanation.surface: Someone describes taking things individually, attributed to Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One by one' looks like a phrase, but splits as I + AGO, then 'one by Shakespeare', a character he wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is the villainous ensign in Othello, a character created by the playwright.

clue.text: A two-sided entry into the border of the Cotton Club scene

indicators.note: entry into says the first pieces go inside the word for border

parts.note: a hem is a border on cloth
R and L, right and left, are the two sides

explanation.surface: A double-sided piece placed into the edge of something about a famous nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cotton Club was a celebrated jazz club in New York's Harlem.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cotton Club was a famous jazz-age nightclub located in this New York neighbourhood.

clue.text: See 25
Popish plotter, mischief-maker among certain Chartists!

indicators.note: among says the mischief-maker is placed in the midst of the map makers

parts.note: OS, the Ordnance Survey, is the British mapping agency, so its staff draw charts
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A conspirator against the Pope causing trouble among nineteenth-century political reformers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chartists' suggests the 1830s British reform movement; here they make charts, i.e. maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Oates fabricated the so-called Popish Plot of 1678, an alleged Catholic conspiracy against Charles II.

clue.text: Redgrave in "As You Like It", finding right change outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for change goes round the letter for right

parts.note: coin is loose change

explanation.surface: An actor's appearance in a Shakespeare comedy, getting a change of the right sort.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition covers two things: Corin Redgrave the actor, and Corin the old shepherd in As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Corin is the first name of the actor Corin Redgrave and of a shepherd in Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: In the Solent I certainly need a siren

indicators.note: In says the letters are found inside the following run of words

explanation.surface: Someone sailing the Solent, a channel off southern England, wants a warning horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'siren' looks like an alarm on the water, but is the seductive temptress of myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a seductive woman who lures others, just as one who tempts does.

clue.text: God, sick at heart, returned 10

indicators.note: returned means the whole assembled piece is read backwards
at heart puts the word for sick in the middle of the word for god

parts.note: deus is Latin for god
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A deity, ill to the core, came back disgraced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' and 'returned' together give the reading DEILLUS turned round. The definition '10' points to the answer of 10-down, DISHONOURED.
explanation.definitionFit: A sullied name or reputation is tarnished and stained, as one that has been disgraced.

clue.text: Aha! Concern atassertion involved with this 10

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled up into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation of discovery over a worrying claim tangled up with disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges AHA CONCERN AT ASSERTION (printed run together as 'atassertion'). 'this 10' points to DISHONOURED.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot on one's reputation is exactly what leaves someone disgraced.

clue.text: Our mother with an Ulster accent, heard here?

indicators.note: heard with an Ulster accent says the words are pronounced in the Northern Irish way

parts.note: our ma is a casual way of saying our mother

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish speaker refers to the family's matriarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Armagh is a county and city in Northern Ireland (Ulster), so the place is 'here' where the accent is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark makes the place where the accent is heard stand for the county in Ulster.
